# gitmoap_repository_mirror (Resource)

Keeps this repository equal to a repository on another host: its branches and tags follow the source on an interval, and nobody here pushes to it. Each sync starts the repository's pipelines as a push by you, unless `run_pipelines` is off — every such run is untrusted, and reaches no connection, secret or cache until a Developer approves its commit. The first sync starts at once. Setting it again changes the mirror and makes you the person its syncs run as. Needs a Maintainer of the repository.

The token needs `import:manage` and `import:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_group_by_path" "platform" {
  full_path = "acme/platform"
}

variable "vendor_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

resource "gitmoap_repository" "vendor_sdk" {
  group_id        = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.platform.group_id
  repository_name = "vendor-sdk"
  description     = "A mirror of the vendor's SDK"
  visibility      = "internal"
}

# Follows the vendor's private repository every six hours: its branches and tags move only with
# the source, and nobody pushes to it here. Each change to the mirror makes the account Terraform
# runs as the one its syncs run as. Pipelines stay off: what a sync brings is code nobody here
# reviewed.
resource "gitmoap_repository_mirror" "vendor_sdk" {
  repo_id          = gitmoap_repository.vendor_sdk.repository_id
  source_url       = "https://github.com/vendor/sdk.git"
  token_wo         = var.vendor_token
  token_wo_version = 1
  interval_minutes = 360
  run_pipelines    = false
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repo_id` (String) Repository ID
- `source_url` (String) The source's clone URL, starting `https://`.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `interval_minutes` (Number) How often to sync, in minutes. At least the plan's floor; an hour when left out.
- `run_pipelines` (Boolean) Whether a sync starts this repository's pipelines, as the person who sets the mirror up.
On when left out. Every such run is untrusted until a Developer approves its commit.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) A token that can read the source, when it is private. Kept sealed; never shown again. Or set `token_wo`, to keep it out of the state.
- `token_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Sets `token` without keeping it in Terraform's plan or state: write-only, with Terraform 1.11 and later. Change `token_wo_version` to send it again.
- `token_wo_version` (Number) A number to change when `token_wo` changes, to send it again: Terraform can't tell, since it doesn't keep it.

### Read-Only

- `last_sync_at` (String) When it last synced.
- `last_sync_error` (String) Why the last sync failed.
- `last_sync_result` (String) How the last sync went: `ok`, or `failed`.
- `next_sync_at` (String) When it next syncs.
- `paused_reason` (String) Why it is paused, when it is: `setter_lost_access` (the person who set it can no longer push
here, or closed their account) or `moved_organization` (the repository moved to another
organization, which the token was not sealed for). Either lasts until somebody who can push
sets the mirror again.
- `repository_id` (String)
- `set_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--set_by))
- `source_ahead` (Boolean) Whether the source has moved since the last sync, when that was checked.

<a id="nestedatt--set_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `set_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor, and empty on a redacted one and on an outside author.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor and on an outside author (`imported`).
- `imported` (Attributes) An author who wrote on another host — a work item, a merge request, a comment, a release an import
brought — and whom nobody here is linked to yet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--set_by--imported))
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

<a id="nestedatt--set_by--imported"></a>
### Nested Schema for `set_by.imported`

Read-Only:

- `identity_id` (String) The outside author's id among the organization's imported identities.
- `login` (String) Their login on that host.
- `name` (String) Their name on that host, when it gave one.
- `profile_url` (String) Their profile's address on that host, when it gave one.
- `source_host` (String) The host they wrote on, such as `github.com`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by its repo_id.
terraform import gitmoap_repository_mirror.example "<repo_id>"
```
